edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ἐγὼ γὰρ καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἐν σαρκὶ αὐτὸν οἶδα καὶ πιστεύω ὄντα. [2] καὶ ὅτε πρὸς τοὺς περὶ Πέτρον ἦλθεν, ἔφη αὐτοῖς: Λάβετε, ψηλαφήσατέ με καὶ ἴδετε, ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ δαιμόνιον ἀσώματον. καὶ εὐθὺς αὐτοῦ ἥψαντο καὶ ἐπίστευσαν, κραθέντες τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ πνεύματι. διὰ τοῦτο καὶ θανάτου κατεφρόνησαν, ηὑρέθησαν δὲ ὑπὲρ θάνατον. [3] μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάστασιν συνέφαγεν αὐτοῖς καὶ συνέπιεν ὡς σαρκικός, καίπερ πνευματικῶς ἡνωμένος τῷ πατρί.
pass_a_gloss: [1] For I know and believe that even after the resurrection he is in the flesh. [2] And when he came to those around Peter, he said to them: 'Take hold, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon.' And immediately they touched him and believed, being mingled with his flesh and with his spirit. For this reason they also despised death, and were found to be above death. [3] And after the resurrection he ate with them and drank with them as one of flesh, although spiritually he was united with the Father.
pass_b_english: I know it and I believe it: even after the resurrection he is in the flesh.

When he came to Peter and those with him, he told them, “Take hold of me. Touch me, and see that I am not a bodiless demon” (compare Luke 24:39). At once they touched him and believed, joined to his flesh and his spirit. That is why they despised death. They were found to be beyond its reach.
And after the resurrection he ate and drank with them (Acts 10:41) as a man of flesh, though in spirit he was one with the Father.

choices.why: Present participle after a verb of knowing is most naturally 'that he is'; it carries Ignatius's claim that the risen Christ remains in the flesh.
rejected: was in the flesh (also defensible; see notes)

choices.why: Kept literal; the phrase is not the Lukan wording ('a spirit does not have flesh and bones') and should not be harmonized to it.
The verb means to be mixed or blended; 'joined to' is plain English for that close union with his flesh and spirit.
rejected: being convinced by (ANF; not the sense of κεράννυμι)
mingled with (accurate but stiff in a reading text)

choices.english: found to be beyond its reach
choices.why: 'Above/beyond death' made into an English sentence; no victory metaphor added.
rejected: found its conquerors (ANF; adds conquest image)

anf_compare.notes: Mostly same sense, but ANF renders κραθέντες as 'being convinced', while the Greek verb means mingled/joined; ANF also adds 'conquerors' for 'above death'.

bible_refs.note: Allusion, not quotation: 'touch me and see' matches; 'bodiless demon' does not. Jerome and Origen trace the saying to another source (Gospel of the Hebrews / Teaching of Peter); marked 'compare'.
'we ate and drank with him after he rose' - the same compound verbs synesthiein / sympinein.

notes: Span: whole of Smyrnaeans 3 (sections 1, 2, 3); old ANF span covers the full chapter.
Pack topic: resurrection-body. Same chapter English is shared by every excerpt id on this chapter.
ὄντα could be read 'was in the flesh' (Holmes, Lake); 'is' follows the present participle and matches ANF's 'is so now'. Reviewer to confirm.
Some witnesses read αἵματι for πνεύματι in §2; Lake prints πνεύματι. Not checked against Lightfoot/Funk yet.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] only. Greek «Ἐγὼ γὰρ καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἐν σαρκὶ αὐτὸν οἶδα καὶ πιστεύω ὄντα» matches A «For I know and believe that even after the resurrection he is in the flesh» and B «even after the resurrection he is in the flesh» (present ὄντα kept as is). Negation «οὐκ εἰμὶ δαιμόνιον ἀσώματον» is «I am not a bodiless demon» in both. «πρὸς τοὺς περὶ Πέτρον» is A «those around Peter» and B «Peter and those with him». «κραθέντες τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ πνεύματι» is mingled/joined to his flesh and spirit; disciples remain the ones joined. «διὰ τοῦτο καὶ θανάτου κατεφρόνησαν, ηὑρέθησαν δὲ ὑπὲρ θάνατον» stays despising death and found above/beyond death, not a conquest claim. «συνέφαγεν αὐτοῖς καὶ συνέπιεν ὡς σαρκικός, καίπερ πνευματικῶς ἡνωμένος τῷ πατρί» keeps Christ as the one who ate and drank, concessive spiritual union with the Father. B compare Luke 24:39 and Acts 10:41 sit beside the touch and eat/drink clauses as labeled allusions. Title Risen in the Flesh names the claim. Locked πνεύματι followed; is/was and αἵματι noted, not left open.

All clauses from Locked Greek paragraph 1 are present and accurately rendered in both Pass A and Pass B. Source identity confirmed as Ignatius, Smyrnaeans 3 via lake-1912-loeb-ignatius. Completeness: no omissions, additions, or contradictions. Negation: 'οὐκ εἰμὶ δαιμόνιον ἀσώματον' correctly rendered as 'I am not a bodiless demon' in Pass A and similarly in Pass B. Agency: Christ acts (he said, they touched, he ate) as in Greek. Modality: indicative mood preserved. Doctrine: resurrection body in flesh maintained. Scripture: Luke 24:39 and Acts 10:41 correctly marked as allusion/compare, not direct quote, per notes. Title 'Risen in the Flesh' names the thought. Notes disclose OCR damage (none here) and variants (αἵματι for πνεύματι). Covered source paragraphs: [1]. No uncertainties remain. All checks pass.
